findings.evidence: Earlier user review showed pale body patches under the sweater.
findings.lesson: Mask base-body vertices under garments and review occlusion edges.

findings.evidence: Source inspection found opaque body and garment alpha inputs exported with alpha blending.
findings.lesson: Force solid body and garment Principled alpha to 1.0 before export.

findings.evidence: User review screenshot showed dark bone-like lines crossing neck, cuffs, and fingers in Blender.
findings.lesson: Hide the armature object in the inspection viewport while retaining skinning and rig data.

findings.evidence: User review screenshot showed a body-colored sliver and uneven pants edge below the sweater hem.
findings.lesson: Increase garment overlap and inspect the result in perspective before accepting the candidate.

findings.evidence: User review screenshot showed dark bone-like lines crossing the neck, cuffs, and fingers in the Blender inspection viewport.
findings.lesson: Hide the armature object in the inspection file viewport by default while retaining the skinned rig in the GLB and Outliner.

findings.evidence: User review screenshot showed a visible body-colored sliver and uneven pants edge below the sweater hem.
findings.lesson: Overlap the pants top further inside the sweater and inspect the result in perspective before accepting the candidate.

findings.evidence: Close render showed the neck skin torn away at the sweater collar, with the dark background visible between the head and torso.
findings.lesson: Protect body vertices within 40mm of open garment boundaries; mask only interior garment coverage.

findings.evidence: User review showed bone-like black lines through neck, cuffs, and fingers in Blender viewport.
findings.lesson: Hide armature drawing by default in the visual inspection file without removing the skinned rig.

findings.evidence: Rear-view review shows a visible body-colored strip between the sweater hem and pants top; the trousers do not reach the waist.
findings.lesson: Raise the pants upper edge to the sweater waist/hip coverage and verify the back view after each build.

findings.evidence: Rear-view preview shows two red sweater patches visible through the gray pants where the 100 mm raised waist overlaps the sweater mesh.
findings.lesson: When raising pants inside an untucked sweater, project any pants vertices that protrude outside the sweater surface slightly behind the sweater surface before export.

findings.evidence: Rear-view render of the 100 mm rise shows the raised pants overlap distorting through the sweater in gray/red patches and pale spots.
findings.lesson: Do not move individual pants vertices through the sweater surface; remove only the overlap triangles that lie outside the sweater shell so the sweater remains clean and the pants reach the waist.

findings.evidence: Rear-view render showed a broad skin-colored gap where deleting protruding overlap faces removed coverage but body vertices stayed visible near the pants opening.
findings.lesson: Do not remove all overlap coverage without a matching waist occlusion or a garment asset whose top fits this body and shirt.

findings.evidence: Rear-view review of the high-rise cargo pants shows sweater-colored strips and pale body patches around the shared waistband; the pants reach the waist but the untucked hem intersects it.
findings.lesson: For this high-rise pant and sweater pair, tuck the sweater mesh slightly below the pants top boundary so the pants form the outer layer; avoid extending the pants through the sweater.

findings.evidence: Rear-view close render shows two body-colored patches protruding through the sweater at its lower hem after raising the cargo pants.
findings.lesson: Treat the central lower hem as a covered region for body masking while preserving body vertices near the collar and sleeve cuffs.

findings.evidence: Rear review still shows a visible strip of skin between the full-length sweater hem and cargo pants after trimming the pants waistband to 5mm below the sweater hem.
findings.lesson: Do not use the sweater’s lowest central vertex as a global pants cutoff; measure the rear hem profile or preserve a small concealed pants overlap under the sweater.

findings.evidence: Rear review shows the sweater now overlaps the pants, but a narrow strip of skin remains visible along the waist.
findings.lesson: Keep a deeper concealed pants overlap beneath the intact sweater hem so the hem covers the waistband and body mask removes exposed skin.

findings.evidence: Rear review still shows uneven sweater and pants geometry meeting along the back waistband; the flat global Z trim does not follow the sweater hem profile.
findings.lesson: Derive the pants boundary from the generated sweater’s hem loop so each generated morph is fitted to its own actual garment geometry.

findings.evidence: Rear review of the hem-loop Boolean trim shows small sweater-colored fragments overlapping the pants waistband.
findings.lesson: Place the pants top slightly below the generated sweater hem curve so the intact sweater visibly overlaps the waistband without coplanar edges.

findings.evidence: User close-ups show a dark neck/collar outline and a torn black gap with visible holes across the rear waistband in the current candidate.
findings.lesson: Keep source garments double-sided where winding/open shells require it; validate the curved cutter against garment surfaces and ensure the pants top remains covered by the full sweater hem.

findings.evidence: The generated close render shows a dark cavity at the sweater neck; disabling the body mask removes it and reveals a continuous neck surface.
findings.lesson: Use a larger protected clearance only around the sweater collar opening so neck vertices remain visible without weakening cuff/hem masking.

findings.evidence: With body masking disabled, a skin strip appears between the sweater hem and pants, while the normal render shows that strip as a black gap.
findings.lesson: Extend the pants top above the hem profile by a small measured overlap so the full-length sweater conceals the waistband and body mask does not expose a void.

findings.evidence: The generated manifest reports 211 overlapping shirt-pants triangle pairs concentrated between z=0.875 and 0.931 m at the waist, despite the reduced visible gap.
findings.lesson: Subtract a small solidified sweater shell from the pants after curved hem trimming, then require another intersection measurement and rear render.

findings.evidence: The rear render after subtracting a solidified full sweater shell shows the cargo pants missing from the hips and legs, leaving exposed skin despite only seven measured shirt-pants triangle pairs.
findings.lesson: Do not Boolean-subtract the full sweater shell from all pants; restrict collision resolution to the waist overlap region and verify pants bounds and face counts before export.

enforced_lessons.guardrail: The recipe builder accepts separate pants and shirt fields and rejects the legacy combined clothes field.
The runtime GLB exporter downsizes source images above a 1024-pixel longest edge; the editable .blend keeps source resolution.
The recipe builder sets the Blender armature show_in_front option to false.

viewer_findings.evidence: Blender 5.2.2 imported the current GLB as Human.rig_export with show_in_front=True, even though the source Blender build has this option disabled. GLB does not carry Blender viewport display preferences.
viewer_findings.guardrail: Use tools/characters/prepare_gltf_blender_view.py to create a Blender inspection file with the imported armature's show_in_front option disabled.
